clue.text: Bitter Aussie rockers covering two singles separately

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the band name encloses the single letters
separately says the two letters go in apart, each in a different gap of the name

parts.note: AC/DC is the famous Australian hard-rock band
with singles, two single ones: this gives the first I, I being one in Roman numerals
a single is one, I in Roman numerals: this is the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A sour Australian rock band records cover versions of a pair of singles.
explanation.walkthrough: The two I's go in at different places: one after the A-C, one after the D, so AC/DC becomes AC-I-D-I-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acidic tastes sharp and sour, which is what bitter can mean of flavour.

clue.text: Remains of bird missing part of foot

indicators.note: something missing has been taken away, so the named length is removed from the bird

parts.note: the chaffinch is a common European finch
an inch is one twelfth of a foot, the imperial length

explanation.surface: All that is left of a bird is a piece of its foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like the bird's own leg, but it is the unit of length, and 'part of' it is an inch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is the husk left over after threshing grain, the worthless leftovers.

clue.text: Plan drive to the rear

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
aft means towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An instruction to reverse the car into position.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline of something, a sketch of what is intended.

clue.text: Nearly nothing can be found at bottom of storeroom

indicators.text: can be found at bottom of
indicators.note: in a down entry, being at the bottom of something means coming after it

parts.note: a closet is a small room or cupboard for storing things
the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Almost nothing is left at the back of the store cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to means almost or approximately, as in close to midnight.

clue.text: Squint at hairless horse

parts.note: skew, as in skew-eyed, means looking askew or squinting
bald means without hair

explanation.surface: Someone peering at a horse with no coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewbald is a horse with patches of white and a colour other than black, a coat pattern.

clue.text: Barbarian stifles lake rescue

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the first word closes round the second

parts.note: a savage is an uncivilised brute, a barbarian
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A brute smothers a lake-side rescue attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is saving goods or a vessel from loss, so it is a kind of recovery.

clue.text: Letter records rampaging lion

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: a rampaging animal runs wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A written note mentions albums and a lion on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Made a mistake and ran to suppress articles in Europe

indicators.note: suppressing keeps something held down within, so the first word encloses the articles

parts.note: colours that ran bled, spreading in the wash
UN is a French indefinite article and DER a German definite article

explanation.surface: A runner who ran while banning European goods got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' are grammatical ones from European languages, not objects.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder is to make a clumsy error, so blundered is the past tense of erring.

clue.text: Drunk, with most of gin knocked back, I start to offend American likely to sue

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here it signals the letters are read backwards
all but the last letter of the spirit is kept
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: US is short for United States, American

explanation.surface: A drunk, downing most of a gin, begins to give offence to an American who might take him to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reads like drinking, but it turns GI round to IG.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigious person is quick to go to law, prone to bringing lawsuits.

clue.text: Basis for dressing a boy covered in dirt

indicators.note: being covered in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: soil is earth, dirt
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A grubby boy needs a bath before getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests putting clothes on; it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette and similar salad toppings are made mostly from this kind of oil.

clue.text: Filthy dog kept in small yard

indicators.note: a dog kept in a yard is held inside it, so these letters are enclosed

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A grubby dog confined to a tiny backyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Smutty means dirty in the sense of indecent or soiled with soot.

clue.text: Unusual way to play a squash shot?

definitions.meaning: eccentric or bizarre, as an informal idiom

definitions.text: way to play a squash shot?
definitions.meaning: in squash the ball is played against the walls of the court

explanation.surface: A quirky technique on the squash court.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-wall is slang for wacky, and literally describes a ball rebounding from a wall.

clue.text: Searches for somewhere to stay

definitions.meaning: excavates or rummages to find something
lodgings, especially rented rooms, in British informal use

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig is to search by burrowing; digs is British slang for lodgings, typically a student's rented room.

clue.text: Film cops' internal complaint when current defamation case is thrown out

indicators.note: whatever is thrown out is removed, here letters taken from the ailment

parts.note: a kidney stone is a painful complaint inside the body
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A legal story: police suffer an embarrassing ailment as a libel action is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' and 'case' sound legal, but they give I and the outer letters D and N, taken from KIDNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Keystone Cops were the bumbling police of early silent comedies made by Keystone Studios.

clue.text: What happens in autumn, but not at first, to earwig

indicators.note: the opening letter is not there, so it is taken away

parts.note: in autumn, leaves drop from the trees

explanation.surface: An insect does its thing in autumn, but not straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earwig' looks like the insect that lives in fallen leaves, but it is the verb meaning to listen in.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for listening secretly to someone else's conversation.

clue.text: Feeling sick, to begin with, in South Eastern country

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: the first letter sits inside the country

parts.note: a nation is a country

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is a word's first letter

explanation.surface: Someone feels unwell in a country in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a physical perception or awareness, such as a tingling.

clue.text: Finally, Usain Bolt cramped

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the name

parts.note: a bolt is a crossbow arrow

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, the sprinter, at last seized with cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: Usain Bolt is the Jamaican sprint champion, but 'Bolt' here is a projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means having little width, tight or restricted for space.

clue.text: Cable maybe trailing from electronic display

indicators.note: trailing comes behind, so the name follows the letter

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
Vince Cable is a British Liberal Democrat politician, a former party leader

explanation.surface: A wire hangs out of an electronic screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like a wire, but it is the surname of Vince Cable, a former British cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality clearly.

clue.text: Choose Royal Academy to present Greek tragedy

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA stands for the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: Picking the Royal Academy to stage a classical play.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a tragedy by Sophocles, and also by Euripides, about Agamemnon's daughter.

clue.text: Somewhat similar to Jo or Russell's show?

parts.note: Jo Brand and Russell Brand are both British comedians sharing that surname
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: A question about one of two British comedians' television programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a TV programme but is a verb, to wave something about.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave or flourish something, displaying it boldly.

clue.text: Roll around Lancashire to get sponsorship for one servicewoman?

parts.note: a barm cake is a soft bread roll in north-west England, including Lancashire
aid is support, such as funding a sponsor provides

explanation.surface: Bread-roll sales raise sponsorship for a woman in the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servicewoman' suggests the military; she serves drinks. 'Around' means 'in the region of', not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid is a woman who serves customers at a pub counter.

clue.text: Are guards called to order?

indicators.note: guards stand round something, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A question about whether sentries were summoned to keep discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called to order' is a meeting phrase; split, 'called' is RANG and 'order' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange is to put things in order, sorting or organising them.

clue.text: Where most people are held back in appraisals

indicators.note: held back means sent backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the letters are found inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Staff are being held back after their reviews at work.
explanation.definitionFit: This continent is home to roughly 60 per cent of the world's population.

clue.text: Amplification system surprisingly met with rapture

indicators.note: what turns out surprisingly is not in its expected form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new sound system gets an ecstatic reception.
explanation.definitionFit: This old cone-shaped device was held to the ear to make sounds louder for the hard of hearing.

clue.text: Perhaps Bloomberg at one time could love Republican?

parts.note: may expresses possibility, as could does
love is zero in tennis, looking like O
R is short for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: Speculation over whether Michael Bloomberg once fell for the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Bloomberg was elected as a Republican, which makes the surface fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomberg served as head of New York City's government from 2002 to 2013.

clue.text: German, 25, is stern when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other, here the first two going to the back

explanation.surface: A German entertainer turns severe while out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-across, a painter; ST moves from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born surrealist and Dada painter.

clue.text: Performer's unusual traits

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are not in their normal order

explanation.surface: A performer's quirky characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer such as a singer or musician is called a recording or performing star of this kind.

clue.text: In the year before year one: nothing! — extremely frustrating

parts.note: anno is Latin for in the year, as in Anno Domini
I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sigh that nothing happened in the year before year one, a maddening gap in the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no year zero between 1 BC and AD 1, which makes the surface work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating or exasperating annoys, so it is vexing.

clue.text: European bath with rotating plughole

parts.note: a spa is a bath or resort with mineral waters

indicators.note: turning round makes the word read backwards

parts.note: a drain is the outlet hole for water

explanation.surface: Water swirls down a bathtub plughole.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a native of Spain, a European country.

clue.text: Cheaper ratatouille includes ingredients that need refinement

indicators.note: the words include the letters within them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A budget vegetable stew has ingredients that could be better.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of errors in a printed book that need correcting is given this Latin plural name.
